svg.text: Deal Intelligence — Trust Boundary and Controls
Mo Messidi, Chief Executive Officer, Deal Intelligence
What crosses the production account boundary, and the control applied at each crossing. In through the WAF, out through the NAT.
Verified read-only against the live account, 2026-11-01.
Outside the account
Customers
MCP clients · REST API · Clay
authenticated on every route
PropelAuth
Google SSO · JWT · API keys
identity provider (sub-processor)
Third parties — egress only
customer CRMs · Google Workspace · data vendors
no inbound path into the account
Deal Intelligence AWS account 164482277879 — us-east-1 (production)
CloudFront + WAF — the only way in
TLS 1.2+ · AWS Shield Standard (DDoS)
self-managed WAF: origin verification (direct function-URL hits 403),
shared rate limiting per credential then IP, security headers
NAT instance — the only way out
t3.micro 52.70.24.151 · IMDSv2 · SSM · no key pair
no public ingress; accepts 10.0.1.0/24 and 10.0.2.0/24 only
egress NAT for the private subnets
HTTPS
JWT / API key validation
OAuth · directory · enrichment
Authentication and tenancy
PropelAuth bearer for app users · PropelAuth API keys for MCP and /v1/li
X-Internal-Key header for internal callers — no credential in a URL path
tenant taken from the token; company writes are allow-listed
Private subnets — compute
Lambda app · mcp · batchOrchestrator · documentdb-proxy
scheduled jobs · no inbound path except through CloudFront
DocumentDB — customer and research data
private subnets · TLS · KMS-encrypted · deletion protection
35-day automated backups · 27017 from the Lambda and NAT SGs only
egress
Logging and evidence
CloudTrail multi-region with log-file validation · VPC flow logs · CloudWatch Logs 90 days · S3 with Block Public Access · KMS · Secrets Manager (no secrets in Lambda environments)
No security group in the account allows 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0. Private subnets do not map public IPs.
